Alex (runtime): quick summary — ran Mistral-7B perf sweep: compare GQA vs MQA KV layouts + RoPE scaling tweak (x1.5). found a regression when paged-KV fragmentation crosses ~2MB chunk boundary. throughput drops even though kernel selection shows same code path. :thinking:
Maria (ml-infra): can you paste the numbers? seq lenses, batch sizes, GPU type?
Alex (runtime): GPU: A100-80GB. seq: 512/1024. batch=8 for seq512, batch=4 for seq1024. two runs: (1) GQA flat-KV (no paging) (2) MQA paged-KV w/ shard-layout V2 + RoPE scale. results —
Alex (runtime): ```
run, seq, batch, tokens/s, p99_latency_ms
GQA-flat, 512, 8, 12200, 42
MQA-paged, 512, 8, 10000, 53  <-- ~18% throughput drop, p99 +26%
GQA-flat, 1024, 4, 7400, 88
MQA-paged, 1024, 4, 6100, 110 
```
Alex (runtime): flame shows large time in copy_kv_page() + memcpy hot path, and kernel selection fell back from fused-attn to aten-cuda for some layers due to head dim parity mismatch.
TJ (perf): interesting — did the kernel selector log indicate why fused was rejected? parity or sequence length?
Alex (runtime): selector log: "fused_attn incompatible: heads_per_kv=5 (odd) vs kernel expects even". MQA created heads layout where num_key_value_heads != num_attention_heads / something due to compression. So fused kernel avoided -> fallback.
Maria (ml-infra): that explains part of it. fused->aten usually increases compute but not a 18% multi-ms drop. where's the memcpy/fragmentation come from?
Alex (runtime): paging metadata: when paged layout creates fragments smaller than page_size (2MB), we end up doing many small device->host copies and re-assembling, which kills throughput. The RoPE scale change shifted positional slice alignment so fragment boundary moved. Basically alignment + odd head counts = kernel mismatch + heavier paging.
Sam (infra): do we have a repro that isolates just the paged fragmentation? can we force same head counts to see effect?
Alex (runtime): yes — ran a controlled patch: force num_key_value_heads=8 for all layers (even when MQA would prefer 5) -> fused kernel selected again and memcpy counts drop significantly. numbers: tokens/s for MQA-paged w/ forced-8 -> 11850 (close to flat GQA). so 8 vs 5 is the delta.
TJ (perf): good signal. suggests two mitigations: 1) kernel selector should consider logical coalescing (treat odd kv-heads as if padded to next even) or fallback to a compatible fused kernel variant; 2) adjust paging allocator to enforce fragment alignment to 4MB or coalesce small fragments at runtime.
Maria (ml-infra): padding head counts could cause small quality differences? does forcing 8 change kv dims and embed mapping?
Alex (runtime): forcing only changes internal layout (pad the KV tensors). no change to model weights or attention math (we pad zeros). Verified output eq-check on 50 examples — diffs < 1e-6 except for FP16 rounding. quality fine.
Sam (infra): coalescing small fragments seems safer as a first step — scheduler could merge adjacent fragments into a single device buffer when contiguous. downside: memory bump. what's fragmentation memory overhead?
Alex (runtime): in worst-case we saw +5% resident GPU memory when coalescing small fragments for seq1024. acceptable for dedicated customers but we need heuristics for hosted mode.
TJ (perf): another angle: batching heuristics — if small fragments hit memcpy blowup, reduce concurrency (smaller batches) to amortize copies? did you test variable batch?
Alex (runtime): yes — lowering batch from 8->4 for seq512 improved memcpy peaks but costed throughput. net tokens/s still lower than fixing fused kernel. so it's a bandaid.
Maria (ml-infra): action items?
Alex (runtime): proposed triage: 1) quick fix: kernel-selector padding flag (treat odd kv-heads as padded to nearest even) + metric to detect when fused rejected so we surface in console. 2) medium fix: allocator coalescing and fragment compaction on page commit. 3) long-term: enhance fused kernels to accept odd heads or provide alternative kernels for MQA layout. 4) add regression test to perf-suite that runs MQA layouts with RoPE variants.
TJ (perf): add a perf regression alert when tokens/s drops >10% vs baseline for any model+layout combo. link to run id?
Alex (runtime): I'll open an RFC + PR. infra bot, create perf-regression issue and link baseline plot.
InfraBot: created issue #INFRA-7421: "MQA paged-KV fragmentation + kernel-fallback causes throughput regression" and attached perf run 17825-2026-03-17.
Maria (ml-infra): can you attach selector logs and flame traces to the issue?
Alex (runtime): yes — upload in a minute. also adding a small patch that pads kv-heads to even at allocation time behind a flag `runtime.force_even_kv_heads` (default=false).
Sam (infra): let's gate default on dedicated only for now. hosted customers might care about memory.
Alex (runtime): agreed. I'll make the flag default=true for dedicated, false for hosted, and add console telemetry when we flip it per-customer.
TJ (perf): great. once PRs land, let's run the perf-suite across Llama/Mistral/Mixtral/Qwen configs to ensure no other combos regress.
Alex (runtime): plan to run matrix overnight and post summary tomorrow AM. thanks all :thumbsup:
Maria (ml-infra): :eyes: looking forward to the summary.
TJ (perf): thanks — nice root cause.
